paper.title: Quantum Entanglement Path Selection and Qubit Allocation via Adversarial Group Neural Bandits

unmapped: R groups of arms (paths); within each group a finite set of arms in R^{D_r} with unknown nonlinear reward h_r in [0,1], learned via overparameterized neural network (NTK regime, effective dimension d_tilde)
Adversary chooses binary attack vector a^t over groups each round; realized success rate s^t = a^t(r) h_r(x)
Observation is Bernoulli Y^t with mean s^t; attacks are detectable
Comparator: best fixed group in hindsight, with per-round optimal arm within that group (group-static strategy)
settings.definition_quote: We define $R$ groups of arms ... Within each group $r \in \mathcal{R}$, the arms represent various qubit allocation strategies ... the adversary simultaneously chooses a binary attack vector $a^t$ ... $\reg(T) = \sum_{t=1}^T s^t(\gamma, \xi_\gamma^t) - \mathbb{E}[\sum_{t=1}^T s^t(r^t, x^t)]$

conditions: network width m >= poly(T, L, sup D, 1/lambda, log(1/delta)) (sufficiently large)
NTK-based approximation assumptions from Zhou et al. 2020

source.quote: For any $\delta \in (0, 1)$, by choosing $\beta = T^{-1/4}\sqrt{\log(T)}$ and $\eta = T^{-1/2}$, such that for any $\delta \in (0,1)$, if $m, \lambda, \zeta$ satisfy the same condition as Lemma 2, then with probability at least $1-\delta$, EXPNeuralUCB yields the following expected regret bound $\reg(T) = O(T^{3/4}\sqrt{\log(T)})$.

results.notes: Regret is expectation over algorithm randomization, bound holds w.p. 1-delta (over NN init/noise); recorded as high_probability_regret. Hidden dependence on effective dimension d_tilde, R and log(1/delta) is suppressed. Comparator is best fixed group with per-round best arm. Adversary type not specified in theory.

cited_results.setting_description: Pure-adversarial version of the group problem where the optimal arm in each group is known (adversarial multi-armed bandit over groups)
